marie (Customer): Hey team — we started seeing a spike of 429s today when prefetching long user histories + doing concurrent calls to rwd3-large. Each request has ~35–40k tokens in the prompt and we fan out 6 parallel requests per user. Started ~2026-03-16 14:02 UTC, no auth failures, just 429 rate limit responses. Any pointers?

amal (Support): Sorry you're hitting that, @marie. Can you paste one of the failing curl examples and the response headers (if available)? Also approximate QPS/RPS and whether the requests are short bursts or sustained?

marie (Customer): Here's a minimal repro curl we ran from our staging:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-large","input":"<~40k tokens of convo history + user prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```

Response we get (snippet):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-model: rwd3-large
x-rw-rpm-remaining: 0
x-rw-tpm-remaining: 1200
x-rw-concurrency-remaining: 0
retry-after: 8
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per-model RPM exceeded"}
```

This is happening only when the context is large + parallelized. Single requests with same context succeed.

amal (Support): Thanks. That header set is helpful. Two quick clarifications: (1) are those 6 parallel requests coming from the same API key/client IP? (2) roughly how many requests per minute overall?

marie (Customer): Yes same API key. Roughly 180 requests/min per instance (we have 3 instances so ~540 rpm total), but bursts during some user flows are ~30 concurrent in a short window.

raj (Eng): Quick explain on how this ties together: model-specific limits are enforced across three levers — per-model RPM/TPM (tokens/min), max concurrency slots, and a burst window that lets short spikes through until the RPM bucket depletes. Important detail: tokens in the request body (prompt length) count toward TPM and your large context consumes a lot of token budget per request, so the effective requests/min allowed is much lower for those long prompts.

Concretely for rwd3-large (example numbers):
- Configured sustained RPM: ~1000 requests/min across the fleet for shared hosted tier (varies by account).
- Max concurrency (parallel inference slots): ~12 for the shared pool per account.
- Token bucket: TPM counts tokens in+out; a 40k-token prompt + 1k generation is ~41k tokens — so a few parallel such requests will exhaust TPM quickly.

So you saw concurrency_remaining: 0 + rpm_remaining: 0 — both hitting limits. That matches your single-request success (enough tokens for one) but fails when multiple run in parallel.

raj (Eng): Short-term mitigations:
- Reduce parallelism to <= 6 and add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s.
- Trim context: only send freshest 8–12k tokens and store the rest in a retrieval layer or use summarized history.
- Use streaming / chunked generation where possible so the runtime can allocate fewer concurrency slots per active request.
- If latency is critical and you need sustained concurrency with long contexts, request Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) or a quota increase — we can open a support ticket to evaluate.

amal (Support): Can you try a quick repro script? If you can reproduce locally, include request headers + x-rw-* headers and call IDs so we can correlate. Example python loop we usually test with:

```
import requests, time, random
for i in range(10):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-REDACTED'}, json={'model':'rwd3-large','input':'<40k tokens...>','max_tokens':512})
    print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-rw-rpm-remaining'), r.headers.get('x-rw-concurrency-remaining'))
    if r.status_code==429:
        sleep = (2**min(i,5)) + random.random()
        time.sleep(sleep)
    else:
        time.sleep(0.1)
```

If you can paste that output we can look up the backend traces.

ops-bot: Alert — rate_limit_exceeded detected: model=rwd3-large account=marie_corp key=sk-*** at 2026-03-16T14:03:12Z. Current sliding RPM window shows short spike to 680 rpm, token consumption spike to ~1.6M tokens/min.

marie (Customer): Ran the loop — confirm we see 429 after ~4 parallel requests with full context. Output:
```
0 200 12 3
1 200 11 2
2 429 0 0
3 429 0 0
```

So it looks like both RPM and concurrency deplete quickly.

raj (Eng): That's consistent. Two additional notes: (1) TPM accounting is per-minute sliding window — if you have sustained large-token requests, the window doesn't refill quickly. (2) We have an internal burst credit mechanism, but it assumes average token sizes; extremely large prompts consume burst credits instantly.

amal (Support): For next steps I can: (A) open a dedicated quota review with infra to evaluate raising RPM/TPM and concurrency for your account; (B) propose a short-term tapering strategy (reduce parallelism, aggressive caching of prefixes); or (C) help you evaluate Dedicated. Which do you want us to start with?

marie (Customer): Can you open the quota review? We need sustained ~20 concurrent long-context requests with <200ms queuing. Also any quick change we can roll now?

raj (Eng): Opening a quota review is the right move. As a quick change today, add client-side concurrency limit to 4 and implement exponential backoff (retry-after + jitter). That will smooth bursts and avoid repeated 429 spikes while we evaluate Dedicated. Also consider precomputing embeddings/summaries to reduce prompt size.

marie (Customer): Ok will throttle on our side and share logs for the quota ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

amal (Support): Thanks — I've created ticket #INC-2026-482 and attached the ops-bot alert + your sample logs. I'll loop in infra/quotas and update here once they weigh in.

raj (Eng): If you want, I can run a short load test from our staging with a dedicated test key to estimate required slots for 20 concurrent long-context requests — ping me and I'll schedule it.

marie (Customer): Please do, @raj. We'll coordinate a 30-min window tomorrow morning UTC.

amal (Support): Noted. Closing the thread for now, will reopen when infra responds.
